exposure: early gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) diagnosis (before 20 weeks)
late gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) diagnosis (24-28 weeks)
outcome: need for intensive care after birth (maternal)
adequacy of birth timing for gestational age
adequacy of birth weight for gestational age
cohort: The study included 320 women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), diagnosed either early (before 20 weeks) or late (24-28 weeks), who received prenatal care at a hospital in southern Brazil.
finding: Early GDM diagnosis in a low-income population was associated with more prenatal consultations and pharmacological treatment, potentially contributing to reduced adverse maternal outcomes.
mod_finding: The primary composite maternal outcome, which included cesarean section or instrumented vaginal delivery, was more frequent in the late GDM group, suggesting early GDM diagnosis may reduce these adverse birth modes.
